_comment: Frozen denominators and qualitative directions for the canonical synthetic study in canonical_study.R. Every number here was measured from that fixture, not asserted from intent. A code change that moves any of these has changed an analytic decision: either the change is wrong, or this file needs an intentional update in the same commit. Reviewing a diff to this file is reviewing a change to the study's denominators.

roster._comment: Provider-level counts. P13 repeats P01's NPI (same physician, two roster IDs); P16 has no NPI.

calls._comment: One row per call. P04 has two office locations so contributes four calls; P14 has a Medicaid arm only, which is why the arms are 17/16 rather than balanced.

exclusions._comment: Reconciliation: contactable + excluded must equal total calls. Every excluded row carries a reason from the allowed vocabulary; no row is excluded with a blank reason.

outcomes._comment: appointment_offered is deliberately three-valued. The two NA rows (P11) are ambiguous outcomes that were reached but not resolved, and must never silently become FALSE.

denominators._comment: The analytic denominators. These are the numbers that vanish silently when an upstream change drops rows, which is the failure this fixture exists to catch.

acceptance._comment: Proportions to 4 dp. P03 refused the Medicaid call, which is the single non-offer among contactable Medicaid rows.

wait_times._comment: business_days_until_appointment is the primary outcome; calendar days are the sensitivity comparator. Freezing both guards against the two being swapped, which would leave every model still running and every p-value still plausible.

directions._comment: Qualitative conclusions, deliberately not exact p-values. A code change that reverses one of these has changed the study's answer. Exact statistics are free to move within tolerance; the direction is not.

invariants._comment: Relationships that must hold by construction, independent of the specific counts above.
